I'll solve this problem using my knowledge of electronic configurations:

Sodium (Na) is element number 11 in the periodic table. The neutral sodium atom has the electronic configuration: 1s²2s²2p⁶3s¹.

When sodium loses one electron to form the Na⁺ ion, it loses the electron from its outermost shell (3s¹). This means the Na⁺ ion has the electronic configuration: 1s²2s²2p⁶.

Looking at the options:
A. 1s²2s²2p⁶ - This matches the configuration of Na⁺ after losing its 3s¹ electron
B. 1s²2s²2p⁶3s¹ - This is the configuration of neutral Na atom
C. 1s²2s²2p⁶3s² - This would be the configuration if Na gained an electron (which would be Na⁻, not Na⁺)
D. 1s²2s²2p⁸ - This is not a valid electronic configuration as the 2p subshell can only hold a maximum of 6 electrons

Therefore, the correct answer is A. 1s²2s²2p⁶.

[ANSWER]A[/ANSWER]
